segments.text: A sip of tea. A drag of smoke. You think you're relaxing... but inside your body, something is quietly going wrong.
segments.style: Speak in a low, tense documentary voice, almost a whisper, slightly afraid, building suspense

segments.text: Tea hotter than sixty-five degrees doesn't just warm your throat. It scalds the delicate lining of your food pipe.
segments.style: Serious and concerned, lean on the word scalds

segments.text: And at that exact moment, the smoke arrives... and settles right onto that wounded layer.
segments.style: Slow and ominous, a hint of dread

segments.text: A study of over four hundred thousand people found it. Burning hot tea, plus daily smoking, nearly doubled the risk of esophageal cancer.
segments.style: Grave and fearful, short pause before nearly doubled

segments.text: Now, your heart. Nicotine pushes your pulse up. Caffeine pushes your blood pressure up. Together, the hits stack.
segments.style: Urgent and tense, a little faster

segments.text: And here's the trap. Smoke trains your liver to burn through caffeine faster, so smokers crave cup after cup.
segments.style: Intrigued, like revealing a secret, slightly sinister

segments.text: You don't have to quit tea. Just let it cool, and drop the cigarette. Your food pipe will quietly thank you.
segments.style: Warm, calm relief, gentle and reassuring

segments.text: Send this to the one friend who always does both.
segments.style: Friendly and light, with a small smile
